title: Release Sprint Orchestra — KPI & Readiness Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This doc is the lightweight playbook for the upcoming release sprint (aka "Orchestra"). It combines the product-ops readiness checklist, the sprint KPI tracker we will use in shiproom, and a short post-launch monitoring / rollback decision tree.

Scope:
- Focus: hosted API feature rollout + config changes (no infra migration).
- Audience: product-ops (lead), release-engineering, serving-runtime, SRE, GTM (on-call for comms).
- Timeline: feature freeze -> soft launch -> regional ramp -> global enable.

Principles (quick):
- Keep go/no-go criteria binary where possible (pass/fail).
- Surface metrics early and frequently; prioritize sample-size over polish in first 24h.
- One owner per critical path (listed below).

Shiproom Roster (roles):
- Release lead: Maya Chen (product-ops)
- Runtime owner: Jonah Patel (eng-serving-runtime)
- SRE on-call: Liam O'Neill
- Observability/metrics: Ava Martinez (observability)
- Support escalation: Priya Singh (customer-success)
- Legal/Privacy: Emily Park (sec & compliance, on-call)

Key Milestones & Dates:
- Feature freeze: 2026-02-20
- Staging smoke: 2026-02-24
- Canary start (10%): 2026-03-01
- Canary to region ramp (50%): 2026-03-05
- Global enable: 2026-03-10

Pre-launch checklist (must be completed before Canary start):
- [ ] Final PRs merged and release tag created (owner: release lead) — link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pulls
- [ ] Staging smoke tests green (72h) — owner: runtime owner
- [ ] Memory/latency perf regression within ±5% vs baseline — owner: observability
- [ ] E2E billing instrumentation validated (billing events, token counts) — owner: finance-integration
- [ ] Security scan completed and M/M/No findings documented — owner: sec & compliance
- [ ] Communication plan published to #release-room and GTM playbook updated — owner: GTM
- [ ] Support playbook + canned responses drafted — owner: customer-success

Go / No-Go criteria (Canary start):
- Go if all of the following are true:
  * Staging smoke green
  * Latency P95 within target for Canary traffic mix
  * Error budget consumption < 2% in last 60m of staging smoke tests
  * No high severity security findings
- No-Go if any of:
  * Silent or unknown failing checks in observability pipeline
  * Error rate spike > 3x baseline sustained > 10m
  * High manual rollback risk (DB schema/irreversible changes)

KPI Tracker (update every 2 hours during first 48h of Canary; every 4h thereafter until global):
Columns to capture (shiproom board):
- KPI name | Owner | Target (Canary) | Current | Delta vs baseline | Notes/action

Example KPIs (we will track these specifically):
- API success rate | observability | >= 99.5% | 99.8% | +0.2% | --
- API latency P50/P95 (ms) | runtime owner | P95 <= 320ms | 290/310 | -10% | keep an eye on tokenization spikes
- Cost per 1k tokens (estimated, USD) | finance-integration | <= $0.085 | $0.080 | -6% | ok
- Model degradation regressions (quality eval) | research | 0 regressions | 0 | 0 | run eval set hourly
- Support tickets per 1k calls | customer-success | <= 0.5 | 0.2 | -60% | lower than expected
- Config rollback count | product-ops | 0 | 0 | 0 | ideally 0

Notes on measurement:
- All numeric KPIs must be captured from the single source-of-truth Grafana dashboards; do not copy ad-hoc query results into the tracker without a link.
- For quality regressions we rely on the automated evaluation harness (Confluence link above). If automated evals degrade, hold rollout and investigate.

Risk register (short):
- Risk: Autoscales flood with warm-up latencies -> Mitigation: pre-warm job + circuit-breaker in gateway (owner: infra)
- Risk: Billing double-count due to duplicate events -> Mitigation: idempotency keys + finance checks (owner: engineering)
- Risk: Unexpected prompt patterns causing token explosion -> Mitigation: rate-limited endpoints + quota enforcement (owner: product)

Communication cadence (while live):
- Shiproom live update: every 2h first 48h (Slack thread + one-line update to execs)
- Exec summary: EOD 0, 1, 3, 7 days with topline metrics and action items
- Customer comms: pre-drafted notifications in case of rollbacks or degradations (owner: GTM)

Rollback decision tree (summary):
1) Identify signal: error rate spike or P95 > 2x target sustained for 15m -> convene ops (10m)
2) Attempt fast mitigation: reduce Canary traffic to 0% (reroute to previous model) -> if metrics recover in 10–15m, continue with slower ramp
3) If recovery doesn't happen or customer impact is high -> full rollback + incident channel + notify execs + open SEV
4) Post-rollback: capture repro, assign postmortem owner, freeze the change until fix validated in staging

Post-launch monitoring & validation (first 7 days):
- Daily automated quality evals against sentinel prompt set (owner: research)
- Cost delta report aggregated daily and compared to modeled estimates (owner: finance-integration)
- Customer feedback flags aggregated and triaged within 4 business hours (owner: customer-success)

Reminders / informal notes to self (from previous launches):
- Don’t trust single-panel alarms; correlate across logs/traces/infra metrics.
- When in doubt, reduce traffic and buy time for correct diagnosis.
- If a change touches both runtime and billing, run coordination checklist — these are the highest friction failures.

Appendix: quick links and queries
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops/release-sprint-orchestra
- Broken-tests query (staging): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/actions
- Billing sampling query: bigquery://finance.project.dataset.billing_samples

Action items (next 72h):
- Maya: finalize support canned responses (due 2026-02-28)
- Jonah: confirm Canary autoscale policy change works in staging (due 2026-02-26)
- Ava: create the 4-panel shiproom dashboard and make it editable by roster (due 2026-02-25)
- Priya: rehearse two support playbook flows with on-call (due 2026-02-27)

End — keep this doc pinned in the release-room during the sprint.

(If anything here conflicts with legal/regulatory guidance, prioritize sec & compliance and call out for exec review.)
